references.text: Daniel's vision of "one like a son of man" who came with the clouds of heaven and was brought before the Ancient of Days, receiving dominion, glory, and a kingdom. This is the central Old Testament background for Jesus' words about the Son of Man coming in a cloud with power and great glory ([ref:Dan 7:13-14|Daniel 7:13-14]).
The parallel passage in the Gospel of Mark: "Then they will see the Son of Man coming in clouds with great power and glory" ([ref:Mark 13:26|Mark 13:26]).

The parallel passage in the Gospel of Matthew: "Then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in heaven... and they will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of heaven with power and great glory" ([ref:Matt 24:30|Matthew 24:30]).

John's Revelation begins by proclaiming that Jesus is coming with the clouds, and every eye will see him – a clear parallel to Luke's description of the coming of the Son of Man ([ref:Rev 1:7|Revelation 1:7]).

During his trial before the Sanhedrin, Jesus said that from then on they would see the Son of Man seated at the right hand of Power and coming on the clouds of heaven – a direct reference to the same motif ([ref:Matt 26:64|Matthew 26:64]).
At Jesus' ascension, he was taken up while a cloud hid him, and angels promised that he would return in the same way – in a cloud, with power and glory ([ref:Acts 1:9-11|Acts 1:9-11]).

Paul describes the Lord's return where he himself descends from heaven, and believers are caught up in clouds to meet him – an image that corresponds with the Son of Man coming in a cloud ([ref:1 Thess 4:16-17|1 Thessalonians 4:16-17]).
Earlier in the Gospel of Luke, Jesus speaks of the Son of Man coming in his own glory and that of the Father and the holy angels – the same motif of glory and power ([ref:Luke 9:26|Luke 9:26]).

John sees one who looked like a son of man sitting on a white cloud with a sharp sickle – an image of the Son of Man coming in a cloud for judgment, reflecting Luke 21:27 ([ref:Rev 14:14|Revelation 14:14]).

Jesus urges the disciples to watch and pray so that they may be counted worthy to stand before the Son of Man – a direct follow-up to the promise of his coming in power and glory ([ref:Luke 21:36|Luke 21:36]).
